title: MicroSim Type Catalog Explorer
description: A vis-network hierarchical explorer of the MicroSim Type Catalog: a central catalog node, eight color-coded family nodes and eighteen type nodes in lighter tints. Hovering a type shows its library, clicking it shows a definition, the data it needs, an example objective and a near-miss objective from another type, and a Quiz me mode hides the type labels and asks the learner to click the type that fits each example objective.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Educational Technology
MicroSim Engineering
Data Visualization Libraries
Instructional Design

educational.audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners
learningObjectives: The learner will identify the library, the typical data, and one suitable objective for each MicroSim type in the catalog.
prerequisites: What a MicroSim is and what a library is
The parts of a MicroSim folder

dependencies: vis-network 9.1.9 standalone UMD and CSS (jsDelivr CDN)

accessibility.notes: All details appear as plain HTML text in the side panel; navigation buttons allow pan and zoom without a mouse wheel.

controls.label: Quiz me / Stop quiz
controls.action: Hide type labels and ask which type fits an example objective

controls.label: Fit view
controls.action: Fit the whole catalog in the view

controls.label: Nodes

controls.label: Pan and zoom

assumptions: Families and types follow the catalog table in Chapter 4, with the bubble chart, HTML matrix, celebration effects, concept classifier and Docker lab listed as their own types.
limitations: Example and near-miss objectives are the author's teaching examples.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Explorer plus flashcard-style matching quiz (Remember level)
keyQuestions: Which library does each type use?
What data does each type need?
What objective would each type serve well?
commonMisconceptions: A concept map belongs on a Leaflet map because both are called maps.
Every chart of numbers needs Plotly.
Image overlays and verified posters are the same thing.
assessmentOpportunities: Written library and data list for two families
